user.title: Local Web UIs
user.description: Open the web UIs of local devices and sites inside Home Assistant. Devices that link to a local web page (for example ESPHome with web_server) are discovered automatically; other sites can be added afterwards with "Add web UI".

abort.single_instance_allowed: Local Web UIs is already set up.

init.title: Local Web UIs options

data_description.discovery: List devices whose integration links to a local web page (their "Visit" link), such as ESPHome devices with web_server, WLED or printers.
data_description.link_device_pages: Point the "Visit" button of devices with a web UI at their web UI here, so it also works away from home. To change it for one device, use ⋮ on its row in the Local Web UIs panel. Turning it off restores the original links.
data_description.linked_devices: Next to each device with a web UI, add a device named after it with "web UI" appended. It appears in the "Linked devices" card of the device's page, and its "Visit" button opens the web UI here. The device itself is not changed.
data_description.panel_title: Name of the Local Web UIs entry in the sidebar. Leave empty for "Local Web UIs".
data_description.panel_icon: Icon of the Local Web UIs entry in the sidebar.

init.description: These settings apply to all web UIs. Settings of one web UI (hiding it, its device's "Visit" button, forgetting its saved logins) are in the [Local Web UIs panel]({panel_url}): open ⋮ on its row. Web UIs you add ("Add web UI") are edited here, on the integration page.

user.title: Add a web UI
user.description: Any web page your Home Assistant server can reach: a device, a router, a printer, another server.

data.name: Name
data.trusted_acknowledged: I understand that a trusted web UI gets full administrator control of Home Assistant

data_description.url: The full address of the page, including http or https and the port if it is not the default.
data_description.mode: Isolated (recommended) keeps the page away from Home Assistant: it cannot read Home Assistant's data or act as you. Trusted runs it with Home Assistant's own origin, which a few pages need (for example ones using IndexedDB). A trusted page's scripts get full administrator control of Home Assistant, so only use it for pages you fully trust.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn off for devices with self-signed certificates.
data_description.username: Optional. Sent as HTTP Basic authentication so you are not prompted.
data_description.password: Optional. When editing, leave empty to keep the stored password.
data_description.show_in_sidebar: Add a sidebar entry that opens this web UI directly.
